question.text: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, the CSR spending obligation for qualifying companies is set at what percentage of net profits?

answer.text: 1% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years
2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years
2.5% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 5 financial years
5% of the average net profit of the last 1 financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 requires every qualifying company to spend at least 2% of the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years on CSR activities. The base on which 2% is applied is therefore a 3-year average — not the latest year's net profit, not a 5-year window, and not a higher percentage like 2.5% or 5%. The Trap: Options A (1%) and C (2.5%) misstate the statutory rate. Option D (5%) is fabricated and also uses a single-year base. Only the 2% on 3-year average net profit framing matches the Section 135 mandate. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook confirms the legal mandate on CSR spending of 2% of company net profit, but the cited pages do not spell out the "average net profit of the immediately preceding three financial years" formula in full. That specific framing is taken from Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 itself rather than from the workbook pages checked.
